title: Aircrew of Wellington R1801
memorial_details: Large, granite stone with a rectangular bronze, dedicatory plaque. This is located beside a decorative, black, metal bench, which depicts 3 airmen and a Wellington bomber. An RAF crest in relief is at the top of the plaque and a coloured RAF crest is located top-centre of the back of the bench.
inscription: AT 16:05 HOURS ON 7TH OCTOBER 1942, AND RAF WELLINGTON BOMBER PASSED/LOW OVER THIS PLACE. ON A ROUTINE TRAINING FLIGHT, IT RAN INTO DIFFICULTY/ SOON AFTER TAKE OFF FROM RAF WYMESWOLD./ AS THE CREW FOUGHT TO KEEP THE AIRCRAFT IN THE AIR IT WAS SEEN PASSING/ LOWOVER THE ROOF OF BEAUMANOR HALL, JETTISONING FUEL AS IT WENT./ EYWITNESSES SAW IT CLIPA TREETOP AND NARROWLY MISS THE STEEPLE/ OF ST MARY IN THE ELMS CHURCH BEFORE COMING DOWN NEARBY./ WORKMEN FROM BEAUMANOR, PASSENGERS FROM A PASSING BUS AND VILLAGERS RAN TO GIVE ASSISTENCE, BUT THE AIRCRAFT WAS SOON ENGULFED IN/ FLAMES AND EXPLODING MUNITIONS. THE VALIENT CREW OF THREE WERE ALL LOST./(names)/ IN GREATFUL REMEMBRANCE FROM LOCAL PEOPLE;/ WENT THE DAY WELL?/ WE DIED AND NEVER KNEW,/ BUT, WELL OR ILL, FREEDOM, WE DIED FOR YOU
community_connection: Workmen From Beaumanor, Passengers From A Passing Bus And Villagers
